To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exposure to BDZ receptor ligands in late gestation alters brain 31P-NM spectra in the adult offspring.
exposure of the developing rat brain to ligands acting on benzodiazepines binding sites during the third trimester of gestation alters brain high energy phosphate metabolism in the adult rat.
prenatal exposure to benzodiaepine ligands altered brain31P-NMRS in young adult rats in a dose- and site-specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of early developmental influences on the long-term organization of the brain.
the long term influences on the developing brain of drugs acting at BDZ receptors.
the long term effects of early exposure to ligands of BDZ receptor sites on the organization of brain energy metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the developmental exposure to BDZs induces a decrease in brain intracellular pH and changes in phosphocreatine utilization that may be related to a predominant interaction of these compounds with the central-type BD2 receptor.
the effects of the BDZ ligands on brain energy metabolism are not due to a direct interaction with energy producing enzymes or the energy producing pathways.
the effects of prenatal exposure to BDZs are not limited to the brain and that they are not restricted to effects on the central BDZ receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

exposure to BDZ receptor ligands in utero can have lasting influences on intracellular phosphate metabolism in adult offspring, that these effects are mediated by central-type BDZ receptors, and that the peripheral-type receptors can modulate these influences.
the central-type BD Z receptor sites are the predominant sites of action for BDZ ligand effects on brain phosphate metabolism during development.
prenatal exposure to BDZs alters the long-term organization of brain metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prenatal exposure to BDZs may have a lasting impact on brain function and that the effects are mediated through the BDZ receptors.
the developing brain is highly sensitive to perturbations in its environment.
early developmental exposure to BDZ drugs alters brain high-energy phosphate metabolism in adult offspring.
